tasks.short: I check and file personnel documents so each employee’s record is complete, current and accessible to the right people.

today.trigger: A manager, employee, recruiter or training coordinator submits a personnel document or changes an existing one.
steps: Find the employee and relevant case in AFAS, then collect the document from Outlook, Teams or SharePoint.
Check completeness, dates, signatures, document type and the applicable CAO or policy.
Compare relevant details with AFAS and, for training evidence, Studytube.
Ask the sender to correct missing or conflicting information.
File the approved document with appropriate access and update its status.
drudgery: Renaming attachments and finding the correct employee folder
Comparing the same dates and names across documents
Checking repeatedly for missing signatures
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are inconsistent submissions and repeated checks across systems; the actual split needs observation.

lenses.faster: Extract document fields, suggest the employee and document category, and show discrepancies together. Manual renaming and routine comparisons largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An upload starts completeness checks and prepares a filing proposal. Sensitive documents and uncertain matches wait for my approval.
lenses.ambitious: Check every active file for missing evidence and upcoming certificate expiry, rather than discovering gaps during an audit or shift allocation.
lenses.joy: Remove attachment sorting and repetitive checking. I spend more time helping people resolve awkward cases and improving submissions.
lenses.options: Show possible document categories and employee matches with supporting evidence. Offer correction requests tailored to the actual missing information.
lenses.altitude: I maintain the document checklist, access rules and exception queue, and improve the submission process when the same errors recur.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: certificate evidence checks
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: personnel document quality checks
HR Business Partner: administrative preparation of case files

tasks.human_edge: Recognising sensitive grievances, disputed performance records and documents whose meaning cannot be settled by matching fields.
tasks.pattern_why: Document extraction is an llm_step within a workflow; rules check completeness, but a person approves the filing and any proposed record change.

in_practice.trigger: A document arrives through an approved intake form or restricted document library.
steps: Create a case ID and check file type, sender authority and permitted document category.
Extract necessary fields and link them to the source passages; propose an employee match.
Compare fields with AFAS and approved document requirements, flagging ambiguity and conflicting versions.
Present the source document, proposed filing location, access group and corrections for approval.
File the approved version and record the result; route unresolved cases to the responsible HR colleague.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves each filing proposal. Grievance, performance and disputed leave documents also require the responsible HRBP’s review where policy requires it.
systems: Studytube authorised export or verified integration
Proposed Power Automate and AI Builder, subject to licensing and configuration
data_needed: Employee identifiers and authorised case ownership
Document requirements by event and applicable CAO
Access and retention rules by document category
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier history and a restricted workflow log containing document reference, proposed changes, approver, version and outcome.

evidence.claim: AI Builder can extract document fields and provide field confidence scores in Power Automate.
Power Automate supports approval flows triggered by documents added to SharePoint.
The proposed Noordhaven workflow, 45% labour saving and 1.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested estimates.

risks: An incorrect employee match could put a sensitive document in another employee’s file.
Extraction confidence does not establish that a document is accurate, valid or properly signed.

Employer files must exclude diagnoses and medical narratives; keep medical records with the bedrijfsarts or arbodienst. [AP employer guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers)
Extra copies in workflow logs could defeat access restrictions or retention rules.
research_questions: Which document types account for most handling time, and how many already arrive through structured AFAS workflows?
Can the proposed workflow identify the correct employee and document version reliably on a representative sample from all three sites?
What review time and error rate remain after extraction, including grievance and performance documents?
Do the available AFAS and Studytube interfaces support the required references without creating duplicate files?

tasks.short: I keep employee details accurate in AFAS and make sure approved changes reach the right records.

today.trigger: An employee submits a detail change, or an authorised source supplies an approved employee data update.
steps: Collect the change request and identify the employee.
Check the source, approval, effective date and existing AFAS value.
Enter or import the approved data, avoiding changes to fields owned by Payroll or another specialist.
Check the saved result and reconcile any relevant extract.
Confirm completion or return discrepancies to the data owner.
drudgery: Copying approved values from forms or spreadsheets
Rechecking identifiers and effective dates
Explaining differences caused by the nightly dashboard refresh
today.time_sinks: Likely time goes into re-entry, reconciling conflicting sources and correcting identifiers; data already maintained automatically offers little additional saving.

lenses.faster: Validated changes move from approved forms to AFAS without retyping. I review rejected rows and conflicts instead of every field.
lenses.autonomous: An approved change triggers a rule-based update and read-back check. Only allowed fields from authoritative sources qualify.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile employee identifiers, sites, departments and reporting lines daily, improving the records behind onboarding and HR dashboards.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive typing and spreadsheet comparisons. I resolve the few cases where people or systems disagree.
lenses.options: Show the current value, requested value and conflicting sources together. Offer hold, correction or escalation rather than guessing.
lenses.altitude: I own field definitions, source ownership and reconciliation rules, with the HRIS Analyst maintaining the technical integration.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: routine master data reconciliation
Payroll Specialist: preparation of approved input changes
Controller: checks on approved employee cost centre mappings

tasks.human_edge: Knowing who is authorised to change a field and recognising when an apparently simple correction affects pay or employment rights.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured approved changes can be validated, mapped and checked with rules. A model is unnecessary for the record-writing step.

in_practice.trigger: A structured change is approved in AFAS or received from an agreed authoritative source.
steps: Validate employee ID, source authority, allowed fields and effective date.
Check whether the event has already been applied and whether another change conflicts with it.
Write eligible changes through the verified AFAS interface; hold protected or inconsistent fields.
Read back the record and compare it with the approved request.
Notify the requester of completion and place failures in the administrator’s exception queue.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine allowed updates need no additional approval after source approval. Pay, bank details, termination reasons and disputed absence or performance data retain their designated approval controls.
systems: AFAS Profit GetConnectors and appropriate UpdateConnectors
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change history plus a restricted integration log recording event ID, source approval, changed fields, previous values, read-back result and failures.

evidence.claim: AFAS AppConnectors control which GetConnectors and UpdateConnectors an integration token can use.
AFAS provides employee updates through KnEmployee and directs personal-data changes to KnPerson.
The proposed field controls, 70% labour saving and 3 times end-to-end speedup require local testing.

risks: A wrong source-of-truth rule could overwrite a correct record with an outdated value.
Retries or effective-date errors could duplicate or backdate changes.
Production and performance information must remain approved factual inputs, without inferred employee ratings.
Power BI is refreshed nightly and cannot confirm that a live AFAS write succeeded.

Absence updates must contain only permitted employer information. [AP employer guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers)
research_questions: How much re-entry remains after existing AFAS self-service and imports?
Can every proposed field be mapped to an authoritative source and an authorised approver?
Do AFAS interfaces support the required fields, effective dates and read-back checks in Noordhaven’s configuration?
Does a pilot achieve the saving after reconciliation, rejected rows and correction work are included?

tasks.short: I record approved hires, leavers, leave, transfers and promotions in AFAS with the right dates and supporting records.

today.trigger: A manager or HR colleague approves an employment event.
steps: Collect the approved event, effective date and supporting records.
Check the applicable CAO, contract, department, hours and required approvals.
Prepare the related AFAS contract, position or leave changes.
Check consequences with Payroll and other responsible colleagues.
Save the approved event and confirm that required follow-up tasks have owners.
drudgery: Entering the same effective date in several records
Reconstructing an approval trail from messages
Remembering downstream notifications
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are incomplete approvals, linked records and payroll cut-offs; waiting for a decision remains outside administrative automation.

lenses.faster: One approved event populates all proposed AFAS changes and follow-up tasks. Repeated entry and manual checklist assembly disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved event starts preparation and validation automatically. Employment and pay consequences wait for the responsible person’s sign-off.
lenses.ambitious: Check every transfer and promotion for training, manager, cost centre and onboarding consequences before the effective date.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated data entry and chasing routine handovers. I help employees and managers understand what their change requires.
lenses.options: Show what happens if the effective date falls before or after payroll cut-off. Compare permitted contract or schedule variants only when a specialist has supplied the rules.
lenses.altitude: I maintain event checklists and track whether each handover completed, rather than treating the AFAS update as the end of the task.
reach: Payroll Specialist: preparation of approved event inputs
Learning and Development Specialist: transfer-related training administration
HR Business Partner: tracking completion of approved personnel actions

tasks.human_edge: Recognising exceptions in CAO coverage, disputed changes and cases where a correct system entry would implement an unauthorised decision.
tasks.pattern_why: Several linked records and teams are involved. Software prepares and checks the event, but a person approves consequential changes before posting.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised HR event is approved with an effective date and event owner.
steps: Create an event case and retrieve the current AFAS records and applicable checklist.
Prepare linked changes and check effective dates, required fields and conflicting future events.
Show the before-and-after records and downstream effects to the required approvers.
Post approved changes using supported AFAS operations and verify each result.
Create follow-up tasks and keep the case open until failures and required handovers are resolved.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator checks the complete event; the HRBP approves employment terms and Payroll approves pay consequences under existing authority rules.
systems: Studytube verified integration or controlled task handover
data_needed: Applicable CAO and approved employment rules
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS event and change history, with a restricted case log linking approvals, posted records, failed steps and completed handovers.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents employee, contract, salary, roster and function operations through its employee connector.
Power Automate supports workflows with approval actions and subsequent updates.
The complete event workflow, 65% labour saving and 2 times end-to-end speedup are untested estimates.

risks: Some records may update while another operation fails; completion must be checked across the event.
Wrong CAO coverage or effective dates could affect pay, leave entitlement or contractual rights.
A termination reason must come from an authorised decision, never a model’s interpretation of correspondence.

For sickness-related events, automate administrative deadlines while retaining accountable case ownership. [UWV steps during sickness](https://www.uwv.nl/nl/ervaringsverhalen/stappenplan-wet-verbetering-poortwachter?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)
research_questions: Which event types are already handled by AFAS workflows, and where does manual work remain?
Can supported interfaces apply all linked changes and safely recover from partial failure?
Do the two CAOs and payroll cut-offs translate into approved, testable rules for the selected events?
Does the pilot reduce elapsed event completion time as well as administrator handling time?

tasks.short: I check applications for required information and job requirements, then give the recruiter a clear, evidence-based briefing.

today.trigger: An application arrives in Recruitee or the recruiter requests an initial administrative review.
steps: Read the application and the vacancy’s approved requirements.
Locate evidence of relevant qualifications, certificates and stated availability.
Mark missing or unclear information without treating it as a failed requirement.
Ask approved clarification questions and record the response.
Pass the evidence and unresolved questions to the recruiter for a decision.
drudgery: Finding certificate details in differently formatted CVs
Copying facts into recruiter notes
Writing repeated requests for missing information
today.time_sinks: Likely time goes into varied CV formats and missing evidence; recruiter decisions and candidate response delays remain.

lenses.faster: Prepare a requirement-by-requirement evidence table with CV references. I check the originals instead of repeatedly searching and copying.
lenses.autonomous: A new application can trigger a draft briefing and missing-information checklist. It cannot reject, rank or move a candidate based on model judgement.
lenses.ambitious: Give every applicant a consistent completeness check, including applications for warehouse roles that arrive with limited formal CV detail.
lenses.joy: Remove formatting and copying. I spend more time clarifying applicants’ experience and helping the recruiter see transferable skills.
lenses.options: Suggest several neutral clarification questions or interview prompts. Show evidenced, unclear and missing requirements separately.
lenses.altitude: I maintain an intake checklist and audit whether briefings omit relevant evidence or disadvantage particular application formats.
reach: Recruiter: application completeness checks and briefing preparation
Learning and Development Specialist: identification of certificates needing verification

tasks.human_edge: Understanding transferable experience, recognising bias in requirements and giving an applicant a fair opportunity to clarify ambiguous evidence.
tasks.pattern_why: The model organises evidence and drafts questions while the administrator and recruiter remain responsible for eligibility assessment and candidate treatment.

in_practice.trigger: A new application is available in Recruitee for a vacancy with approved intake criteria.
steps: Retrieve only the application content and approved requirements needed for the review.
Draft an evidence table with source passages and mark absent information as unknown.
Have the administrator check every relevant claim against the original application.
Prepare approved clarification questions for human review and sending.
Record the verified briefing in Recruitee; leave selection and stage decisions with the recruiter.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator verifies the briefing and outgoing questions. The recruiter makes every qualification, invitation and rejection decision.
data_needed: Candidate privacy notice and retention rules
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted Recruitee review notes containing verified evidence, source references, reviewer and decision owner; draft retention follows the candidate policy.

evidence.claim: Recruitee documents webhooks for candidate events that can trigger external preparation workflows.
A language model can draft a CV evidence table, but completeness and faithful citation require human checking.
The proposed review process, 35% labour saving and 1.4 times end-to-end speedup have not been demonstrated at Noordhaven.

risks: A summary can omit relevant evidence or turn missing information into an apparent disqualification.
Name, age, nationality, health and other irrelevant personal information can introduce bias; restrict the briefing to legitimate job requirements.

Human approval alone does not remove EU AI Act high-risk classification if the actual use evaluates or filters applicants. Obtain a use-specific assessment; the Commission reports Annex III high-risk rules applying from 2 December 2027. [SER employment AI guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/belangrijke-themas/ai), [Commission timeline update](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)

A recruiter merely accepting an automated recommendation may fail to provide meaningful human review under the AVG. [AP guidance on automated decisions](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/basis-avg/privacyrechten-avg/recht-op-een-menselijke-blik-bij-besluiten)
research_questions: Can the tool capture relevant evidence equally well from short CVs, multilingual applications and informal work histories?
Do recruiters save time after verifying source passages, or simply inherit extra checking work?
Does the intended briefing materially influence selection, and what AI Act classification and AVG assessment follow?
Can a pilot preserve or improve qualified-applicant progression and 90-day hire outcomes without introducing unfair exclusions?

tasks.short: I answer employees’ and applicants’ questions about requirements, pay, benefits and HR procedures.

today.trigger: An employee, manager or applicant contacts HR with a question.
steps: Clarify the question and whether it concerns a general policy or an individual case.
Identify the applicable CAO, employment arrangement and policy version.
Find the approved answer or ask Payroll, Compensation and Benefits, or the HRBP.
Explain the answer and relevant next step in plain language.
Record any case requiring follow-up and confirm ownership.
systems: AFAS Profit for authorised individual enquiries
drudgery: Answering the same procedural questions repeatedly
Searching for the current policy version
Forwarding questions between specialists
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are policy lookup, unclear CAO coverage and specialist handovers; a wrong first answer can create more work.

lenses.faster: Match routine questions to approved answers with the relevant policy link. I receive exceptions with the question and context already organised.
lenses.autonomous: An authenticated employee question can receive a published routine answer immediately. Individual pay disputes, ambiguous CAO cases and sensitive matters go to a person.
lenses.ambitious: Provide consistent HR help across shifts and sites, with clear language versions approved for common questions.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated policy searches. I have time for people who need explanation, reassurance or a difficult case resolved.
lenses.options: Offer a short answer, a fuller explanation or a step-by-step guide using the same approved content.
lenses.altitude: I maintain the answer library, review unresolved questions and ask policy owners to fix recurring gaps.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: routine benefits information
Recruiter: standard application-process questions
Payroll Specialist: routine payslip navigation and process guidance

tasks.human_edge: Noticing distress, disagreement or a question whose wording hides a sensitive personal situation.
tasks.pattern_why: A model maps varied wording to an approved answer within a controlled workflow. Rules restrict scope, authentication and escalation; it does not determine individual entitlements.

in_practice.trigger: A question is submitted through an authenticated employee channel or a separate applicant channel.
steps: Identify the audience and ask for non-sensitive clarification when CAO or worker category is unclear.
Retrieve only current approved answers available to that audience.
Return an approved answer with its source and effective date when the question falls within the allowed scope.
Route conflicting, personal or unsupported questions to HR with a minimal case summary.
Review unanswered topics and have the relevant policy owner approve answer-library updates.
in_practice.human_gate: Policy owners approve answers before publication. A person handles individual entitlements, complaints, pay disputes and every case outside the published scope.
systems: Proposed Copilot Studio with verified authentication and licensing
Existing assisted channels for shift workers without suitable digital access
data_needed: Approved answers by employee, agency-worker and applicant audience
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted HR enquiry log containing topic, answer version, source, escalation and outcome; redact unnecessary personal details and minimise transcript retention.

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio supports SharePoint knowledge sources and retrieval governed by the authenticated user’s permissions.
Restricting automatic responses to published routine answers is a plausible design, requiring additional scope and escalation controls.
The proposed service, 55% labour saving and 2 times end-to-end speedup are scenario estimates.

risks: Applying the transport CAO answer to a warehouse employee or agency worker could misstate rights.
Permission-aware retrieval does not ensure that an answer is correct or that the source is current.
Many shift workers and external applicants may lack the authentication required for the employee service; preserve accessible human channels.
A conversational service must be clearly identified as automated and offer an easy human handover.
A model must not calculate or decide an individual’s pay, benefits eligibility or legal entitlement through this enquiry service.
research_questions: What proportion of actual enquiries can be answered from a stable, approved answer library?
Can shift workers access the service securely during their normal working pattern?
Does testing reliably route ambiguous CAO questions, disputes and sensitive cases to a person?
Do resolution time, repeat-contact rate and employee satisfaction improve after specialist handovers are counted?

tasks.short: I turn an approved hire into a signed, accurate starter file and a coordinated first week.

today.trigger: The recruiter and hiring manager approve a hire and the candidate accepts the agreed offer.
steps: Collect approved terms, starter details and the planned start date.
Check the applicable CAO, contract template and required identity and work-authorisation evidence.
Prepare the contract and starter forms for authorised review and signing.
Create or complete the AFAS starter record and hand approved payroll inputs to Payroll.
Coordinate manager, site and training tasks and chase missing starter items.
drudgery: Copying accepted offer details into forms
Assembling the same starter checklist
Chasing signatures and onboarding owners
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are missing starter information, signing delays and handovers; faster paperwork alone cannot make a hire productive.

lenses.faster: Use the approved offer once to prepare the contract, AFAS proposal and onboarding checklist. Repeated entry and checklist assembly disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted-offer event starts preparation and assigns tasks. The contract and starter record wait for the appropriate approvals.
lenses.ambitious: Give each hire a tracked path through week one and day 90, including training readiness and manager confirmation of productivity.
lenses.joy: Remove copying and routine chasing. I help new starters feel expected and resolve practical first-day problems.
lenses.options: Compare feasible start dates against payroll cut-off, induction sessions and manager availability. Contract choices remain within approved templates and specialist guidance.
lenses.altitude: I own starter readiness and handover quality across the three sites, using incomplete onboarding and day-90 outcomes to improve the process.
reach: Recruiter: administration after offer acceptance
Learning and Development Specialist: onboarding enrolments and completion tracking
HR Business Partner: scheduling and tracking day-30 and day-90 check-ins

tasks.human_edge: Checking the legitimacy of employment terms and documents, reassuring the new starter and securing real commitment from the receiving manager.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow prepares documents and coordinates several systems, while authorised people approve employment terms, identity checks and payroll inputs.

in_practice.trigger: A verified Recruitee event indicates an approved accepted offer; agency placements use a separate approved intake.
steps: Retrieve approved terms and identify any existing AFAS person or employee record.
Request missing starter information securely and prepare documents from the applicable approved template.
Present contract terms, identity-check status and AFAS changes for the required approvals.
After approval and required signing, create or update the starter record and issue named onboarding tasks.
Track week-one completion and schedule day-30 and day-90 checks, escalating readiness gaps to the manager.
in_practice.human_gate: The authorised HR signatory approves the contract; trained staff perform required identity and work-authorisation checks; Payroll approves its inputs and the site manager confirms operational readiness.
systems: Recruitee webhooks and verified API access
SharePoint approved templates and secure intake
Studytube verified interface or controlled enrolment handover
data_needed: Applicable CAO and approved contract template
Starter identifiers and required verification status
Site, manager, shift and start date
Onboarding owners and day-90 outcome definitions
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee handover reference, AFAS starter dossier and a restricted onboarding case log linking approvals, signature status, task completion and manager-confirmed outcomes.

evidence.claim: Recruitee webhooks can notify connected systems about candidate stage changes.
AFAS supports creating employee records with linked employment information through its employee connector.
The proposed hiring handover, 55% labour saving and 1.3 times end-to-end speedup are untested; candidate and manager delays remain.

risks: A pipeline stage may change before the offer or terms are final; the trigger must verify approval and acceptance.
Incorrect templates or CAO coverage could create invalid or unintended terms.
Identity documents and BSN must stay in the authorised process and be excluded from general model prompts and routine logs.
Agency workers require an agency-placement process and must not be treated automatically as direct employees.
Course completion alone does not prove competence or authorise forklift or other safety-critical work.
research_questions: Are accepted offers structured and approved consistently enough to generate starter records without re-entry?
Which delays come from HR handling, candidate signing, verification, training capacity or manager readiness?
Can all three sites provide named onboarding owners and reliable completion evidence?
Does the pilot improve week-one completion and the share of hires productive and retained at day 90?

tasks.short: I find the right employee-file facts and provide an authorised answer or briefing for a personnel action.

today.trigger: An authorised colleague asks for employee-file information or evidence supporting a proposed personnel action.
steps: Clarify the request, intended use and requester’s authority.
Search AFAS and the relevant restricted documents.
Check dates, versions and conflicts between records.
Prepare the necessary facts with source references.
Review the disclosure and send it securely to the authorised recipient.
systems: Studytube when training evidence is relevant
drudgery: Opening many files to find one date or clause
Building timelines from separate records
Copying facts and source references
today.time_sinks: Likely time goes into searching and establishing which record is current; unclear authority or contradictory evidence still requires human work.

lenses.faster: Retrieve relevant facts and draft a source-linked timeline. I verify the evidence and disclosure instead of opening every file.
lenses.autonomous: An authorised request starts retrieval and briefing preparation. The result remains inside the HR review queue until I approve release.
lenses.ambitious: Prepare consistent evidence packs for routine personnel actions, showing missing and conflicting records before a decision is made.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive searching and copying. I focus on resolving contradictions and helping colleagues understand the record.
lenses.options: Offer a brief factual answer, a dated timeline or a document checklist, all based on the same verified sources.
lenses.altitude: I improve file structure, access controls and evidence standards so future enquiries are easier to answer correctly.
reach: HR Business Partner: factual case chronology preparation
Payroll Specialist: approved contract-history retrieval
Learning and Development Specialist: training evidence retrieval

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the requester actually needs, whether disclosure is appropriate and when a factual extract could mislead without context.
tasks.pattern_why: Retrieval and summarisation can run automatically, but sensitive disclosure and evidence used in personnel actions need a meaningful human check.

in_practice.trigger: An authenticated requester submits a defined purpose and employee reference through a controlled HR request.
steps: Check the requester’s authority and restrict the query to the necessary fields and documents.
Retrieve current AFAS facts and authorised document passages with dates and version references.
Draft the answer or chronology, clearly marking missing evidence and contradictions.
Have the administrator verify source support, scope and recipient access.
Release the approved answer securely and record which evidence was disclosed.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every disclosure. The HRBP reviews evidence packs for disputed or consequential personnel actions; the tool makes no recommendation about the employee.
systems: Proposed restricted retrieval and drafting service
data_needed: Requester identity, authority and stated purpose
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted HR enquiry log containing requester, purpose, source references, reviewer, disclosed fields and delivery outcome, without duplicating the entire personnel file.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports scoped data retrieval through configured GetConnectors.
Source-linked summaries of authorised records are plausible, but reliable retrieval across Noordhaven’s files is unverified.
The proposed evidence workflow, 65% labour saving and 2.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested estimates.

risks: An integration account with broad access could reveal records that the requester cannot view; enforce requester-level disclosure rules.
A summary may omit a later amendment, a disputed record or context favourable to the employee.

Medical narratives must stay outside employer retrieval and briefing workflows. [AP employer guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers)
Extending factual retrieval into employee evaluation or dismissal recommendations changes the use and requires a fresh legal and AI Act assessment.
research_questions: Are documents indexed by stable employee and case identifiers, with reliable version metadata?
Can access tests prove that retrieval and release respect requester authority across every source?
Does a representative test retrieve amendments and contradictory evidence without omissions?
How much review time remains for routine enquiries compared with disputed personnel actions?

tasks.short: I collect missing personnel records from employees, managers and agencies and keep track of what is still outstanding.

today.trigger: An HR event, onboarding checklist or file check identifies missing records.
steps: List the missing items and identify the responsible employee, manager, department or agency.
Send a request explaining what is needed, why and by when.
Track responses and send reminders around site and shift working patterns.
Check received items for completeness and correct employee identification.
Pass accepted records into the relevant HR process and escalate unresolved items.
drudgery: Maintaining chase lists
Sending repeated reminders
Matching attachments to outstanding requests
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are unclear ownership, inaccessible channels and late responses; automation reduces chasing effort more than other people’s response time.

lenses.faster: Generate item-specific requests and match secure uploads to the outstanding checklist. Manual chase lists and routine reminder drafting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A missing-item event assigns an owner, sends an approved request and schedules reminders. Disputed, sensitive or overdue cases come to me.
lenses.ambitious: Track completeness for direct and agency starters across all three sites before their first shift, with a named owner for each gap.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive chasing. I help people who cannot use the channel or do not understand the request.
lenses.options: Offer an individual checklist, a manager’s consolidated action list or an agreed agency batch request. Choose reminder timing that fits the shift.
lenses.altitude: I manage collection standards, deadlines and exception routes, and fix recurring reasons records arrive late.
reach: Recruiter: collection of approved starter information
Learning and Development Specialist: missing training evidence collection
Bookkeeper: collection of non-sensitive agency references needed for invoice matching

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a reminder will help, when the request is unreasonable and when someone needs personal assistance or confidential handling.
tasks.pattern_why: Owners, required items, deadlines, reminders and receipt checks can be defined as rules. Content interpretation, filing and consequential decisions stay in their separate reviewed processes.

in_practice.trigger: An approved checklist flags a missing item with a named owner and deadline.
steps: Validate that the item is necessary and select the approved request and recipient channel.
Send a secure upload link or agreed agency request carrying the case reference.
Schedule capped reminders that stop on receipt, cancellation or escalation.
Check receipt metadata and completeness, then hand the item to the relevant verification process.
Escalate overdue, disputed or sensitive items with the collection history.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine approved requests and reminders run without individual approval. The administrator handles disputes, access difficulties, sensitive documents and deadline exceptions.
systems: SharePoint secure intake and request register
Staffing agency portals through verified interfaces or authorised manual handover
data_needed: Named owner and authorised contact details
Deadlines, shift-aware reminder windows and escalation rules
Receipt status and secure upload permissions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted request register linked to the AFAS case, recording requested item, owner, messages, receipt status, reminders and escalation; document contents stay in their authorised destination.

evidence.claim: Power Automate supports event-triggered workflows, email actions and approval handovers.
A shared request register with deadlines and receipt-driven reminders can replace manual chase lists.
The proposed collection workflow, 45% labour saving and 1.4 times end-to-end speedup are untested estimates.

risks: Requests sent to the wrong manager or agency could disclose personal information.
A poorly defined checklist could collect unnecessary documents or health information.
Reminder loops could continue after receipt or overwhelm shift workers; cap reminders and provide assistance.
Agency portal interfaces and external upload access may not support the proposed automation.
Receiving a file proves receipt, not authenticity, validity or readiness for work.
research_questions: Which missing items cause the most chasing, and do they have clear owners and deadlines?
Can employees on every shift and external agencies use the proposed secure collection channel?
Do the three agencies provide supported interfaces, exports or agreed batch processes?
Does the pilot reduce handling time and late records without increasing unnecessary requests or complaints?

role.altitude: The HR Administrator becomes the owner of reliable HR administration: complete records, controlled event processing, clear employee answers and timely handovers. The role designs checks and resolves exceptions, with policy and employment decisions remaining under the designated HR and Payroll authorities.
reach: Recruiter: accepted-offer handovers, application completeness and starter readiness
Learning and Development Specialist: enrolment administration, certificate evidence and expiry follow-up
Payroll Specialist: validated preparation and reconciliation of approved employee changes
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: data-quality rules, exception monitoring and source ownership
HR Business Partner: factual case preparation and administrative tracking of onboarding and absence deadlines
Controller and Bookkeeper: approved cost centre checks and collection of agency reconciliation references
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks represent 728 hours per FTE annually, or 1,456 hours across the two administrators, about 45.5% of the stated role time. The task estimates imply roughly 791 hours of annual capacity released, valued at about EUR 38,000 at EUR 48/hour, before overlap, implementation, licences and ongoing oversight; this is capacity value, not a cash saving. Today’s workflows and anatomy percentages are assumptions for the fictional company. Labour savings measure active handling time; speedups separately estimate elapsed completion time including remaining waits. Document processing, collection, data entry and event handling share steps, so validate boundaries before adding savings. Trust, disputed cases, identity checks and consequential decisions limit autonomy. Changes to personnel, privacy or monitoring arrangements may require OR advice or consent depending on the proposal. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/belangrijke-themas/ai)

role.ambitious_version: Run a consistent administrative path from accepted offer to day 90 across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, with separate appropriate handling for agency placements. Every starter has verified records, named onboarding owners and visible training gaps before work begins; managers confirm productivity and retention at day 90. Use recurring exceptions and employee questions to improve the process, and test whether those improvements raise the share of open roles filled by productive hires who stay.
